prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Modes (Airport Duty Manager=ADM declares; Business Rules Registry holds thresholds/latency/connection protection/gate compatibility/towing priority/stand reopening/turnaround margins/materiality): Normal; Adverse Weather; Capacity Reduction State(extended metering horizon); Recovery Phase(Copperfin-approved; RFM authorizes exit, balances arrival capacity/departure release/stand clearance); Contingency Fallback; Slot Compliance; Winter(MBO confirms). Diversions in Recovery/Contingency. Actors: Regional Flow Manager=RFM(ranks diversions; sees aggregated impact by departure bank/runway stream/airline group), Airspace Sector Planner(Tactical Regulation Proposal), Military Airspace Liaison, Tower Supervisor, ADM(Medical Diversion Notice), Ramp Control Lead, Ground Handling Dispatcher=GHD(baggage reconciliation; sends Towbar Shortage Report when towbars can't support pushback sequence; escalate only if flight in departure horizon or blocks higher-priority movement), Aircraft Operator Rep, Airline Operations Coordinator(confirms on-plan/short deferral/revised departure intent), Slot Coordinator(CTT/TOBT), Network Operations Liaison, Emergency Response Coordinator, Deicing Coordinator, Meteorology Briefing Officer=MBO, Data Governance Steward. Cedarbell=Regional Flow Platform(exceptions filtered/grouped/escalated; record: flight, stand, milestone, recovery time, confidence, accountable role). Parts: Marlinstone=Demand Prediction Service; CAM=Capacity Assessment Module; Arrival Regulation Console; Blueharbor=Slot Allocation Engine(CTT, GDP, Pushback Window Token; uses sanitized readiness); Foxglove=Airport CDM Portal(detailed handler notes for authorized users; prompts mitigation entry in Collaborative Decision Log when exception threatens TOBT/CTT/metering sequence); Common Situation Display(flight impact, severity, recovery window only); Emberline=Departure Metering Service(applies exception only after Registry threshold; CTT→Ironleaf=Tower Sequence Manager, which gets stable readiness indicator+escalation flag); Nightjar(shall suppress arrival handler annotations unless AAR or regulated arrival sequence affected); Halcyon; Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Apron Sensors; Ramp Movement Board(stand-level exception with time band); Gate Conflict Detector; Handling Resource Planner(severity levels, duplicate suppression); Airline Interface Adapter; Sector Load Monitor; Lantern; Alert Distribution

Document units:
S538: The Performance Analytics Warehouse compares escalated exceptions with actual off-block performance to tune severity thresholds and reduce nuisance alerts over time.
S539: During Adverse Weather Mode or Capacity Reduction State, the Business Rules Registry can tighten escalation thresholds for flights close to departure while continuing to suppress low-impact local issues.
S540: If the Regional Flow Platform enters Contingency Fallback State, exception summaries remain available through the Contingency Operations Console with the same role-based visibility rules.
S541: The Data Governance Steward ensures that baggage and handler data exposed outside the local operation is limited to operational necessity and does not disclose unnecessary passenger or workforce details.
S542: Remote stands are used as controlled capacity buffers when contact gates are unavailable, when tow-in sequencing is more efficient than gate holding, or when an aircraft must wait clear of the terminal pier.
S543: The operational concept treats each remote stand as an airside resource with a landside service dependency, not as an isolated parking position.
S544: The Airport Duty Manager publishes the planned remote stand operating posture in the Airport CDM Portal before the first affected arrival bank.
S545: The Ramp Control Lead confirms that each planned remote stand has an assigned aircraft route, safe passenger transfer path, and defined contingency for blocked apron movement.
S546: The Airline Operations Coordinator uses remote stands to protect connection banks only when the resulting passenger transfer time is compatible with the planned departure sequence.
S547: Handling Resource Planner produces the Remote Stand Shuttle Count at regular operating intervals to represent available passenger transfer capacity for remote stand activity.
S548: Shuttle availability is modeled as a finite resource that includes vehicles, drivers, loading positions, terminal curb space, and accessible boarding support.
S549: Passenger bus constraints include maximum load, door cycle time, stand access routing, security segregation, mobility assistance requirements, and the time needed to clear passengers from the aircraft vicinity.
S550: The Ground Handling Dispatcher verifies that bus assignments do not conflict with baggage, catering, fueling, or crew transport movements on the same apron corridor.
S551: The Ramp Movement Board displays remote stand occupancy, expected towing actions, and bus service readiness in a shared view for airside coordination.
S552: The Tower Sequence Manager does not advance an aircraft toward an active departure sequence unless the remote stand release time supports the expected taxi plan.
S553: The Departure Metering Service incorporates remote stand constraints when estimating whether a Target Off Block Time remains achievable.
